pace: 18-20+ mph per the club; 20-22 mph capped at 22 per the shop calendar
visitor_notes: Park in the south lot. The shop says to try the Saturday or Sunday rides first if you are unsure of the pace.
description: An out-and-back morning road ride of about 40 miles heading south from Harris Teeter into Pungo. The club page says 18-20+ mph; the shop calendar lists 20-22 mph with the pace capped at 22 and calls it a drop ride.
evidence: Tripower's home page lists Tuesday/Thursday 7:15 am from Harris Teeter, 2800 Arctic Ave, 40 miles (page fetched Oct 1, 2026); Conte's Southern Virginia calendar lists the Tuesday ride from Sept 15 and the Thursday ride from Sept 3, 2026.

refresh.notes: Tripower home page; the shop calendar feed carries both weekday rides.

name: Thursday Night Millstone Adventure Hour
schedule: Thursdays, gather 5:15 pm, wheels roll 5:30 pm from the Brook St. Garage at the Millstone Trails parking. Lights required.

start_location.name: Brook St. Garage, Millstone Trails parking

visitor_notes: Free. Fill out the 2026 rider waiver online and pick up the sticker at the shop. Helmet and lights required. Check the blog on the day, rain cancels.
description: A weekly mountain bike ride on the Millstone Trails. It opens with a beginner-friendly warm-up loop of 40 to 45 minutes, then continues for another 40 to 45 minutes for intermediate riders. The shop asks riders to make room for BIPOC, women and queer folks.
evidence: The Vermont Bicycle Club blog post of Aug 27, 2026 announces the Thursday Night Millstone Adventure Hour, gather 5:15, roll 5:30, lights required (fetched Oct 1, 2026). Newest post about it is five weeks old.

refresh.notes: The shop posts each week's go or no-go on this blog. Last year the series ran into late October.

name: Vermont Bicycle Shop Pizza Ride
schedule: First Saturday of each month, 4:00 pm sharp, April–October, weather permitting
description: About thirty minutes of the easiest riding Barre has, then pizza. The shop's ride club also runs a weekly women-led beginner MTB hour at Millstone and a weekly training ride; updates go on the club site and Instagram.
evidence: The Vermont Bicycle Club's Pizza Ride page lists a 4 pm start on the first Saturday of each month, April through October, on its 2026 page (next Oct 3); 2026 ride posts run through Sept 24 (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

name: Pride Rides Vermont Group Rides
schedule: Posted date by date on the group's public calendar, mostly on weekend days. 2026 rides so far: Jan 18, Feb 11, May 1, May 30, Aug 9, Aug 14, Aug 15 and 16, Sept 27. The next ride is not posted yet. The time and start are on each calendar entry.

start_location.name: Changes with each ride; see the calendar entry

pace: All levels, per the calendar entries
visitor_notes: Check the calendar for the start and the level of each ride. Some rides are in Vermont and some are not (Aug 9 was in New Hampshire). Cancelled rides, such as Jan 24 in -30 wind chill, are marked on the calendar.
description: A Vermont nonprofit that holds group rides for LGBTQIA+ riders: mountain bike, gravel and road paths. The rides move around the state and are posted one at a time on a public calendar. The group's site says it exists to create a space to ride without having to hide.
evidence: The group's public Google Calendar, embedded on prideridesvt.org, lists Pride Rides on Aug 9, 14, 15, 16 and Sept 27, 2026 (Burlington path ride, 10:15 am roll), and none after that (read Oct 2, 2026).

refresh.notes: The feed also holds old events from 2020 to 2025; read only the future ones. Rides are irregular, about one to three a month in season.

name: GMBC Saturday (VP) Training Ride
schedule: Saturdays, April to fall. Start time and place are announced on the GMBC email list, usually by Thursday, and change through the year.

start_location.name: Announced on the GMBC email list

visitor_notes: GMBC says membership is not required. Sign the club waiver once a season and register for the ride.
description: The club's Saturday training ride. GMBC posts the start, route and weather call to its email list by Thursday and asks riders to register. Lights are recommended all season and routes are on Ride with GPS.
evidence: GMBC's events calendar lists 'Sat VP Training Rides' for Oct 3 and Oct 10, 2026 (fetched Oct 1, 2026). The page gives no start time or pace.

refresh.notes: Calendar entries are all-day with no time. The time is emailed to the club list.

name: GMBC Wednesday Evening Training Ride
schedule: Every Wednesday evening through Oct 24; on the road 6:00 pm May–August, 5:30 pm or earlier in April and September–October (exact time sent to the club email list)
cost: free with a once-per-season waiver; membership optional
description: A 28-mile loop through Shelburne and Charlotte with about 1,150 feet of climbing. Groups of twelve or fewer form by speed; the fastest starts first. Faster groups may not wait. The last group regroups and tries not to leave anyone. You need to hold 15 mph to fit in.
evidence: GMBC's Wednesday training page says the late season, September until 24 October, is on the road at 5:30 pm or earlier, with start times sent to the club email list; its calendar shows October 2026 events (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

name: Ranch Camp Ladies Rides
status_note: The 2026 Ranch Camp ladies series ran every other Monday from June 1 to Sept 28. The shop's site is on its winter layout. Expect it back in June 2027.
schedule: Every other Monday, June–September (2026: Jun 1, 15, 29, Jul 13, 27, Aug 10, 24, Sep 14, 28); 5:30 pm for the Sept 14 ride; free, RSVP on Eventbrite

start_location.name: Rotating trailheads around Stowe; shop at 311 Mountain Rd

cost: free (optional catered food for a fee)
description: Free women's mountain bike rides led by Ranch Camp ambassadors, with LGBTQ+ riders explicitly welcome. Trailheads rotate around Stowe and occasionally Woodstock. Some rides are catered; order food by the Friday before. Sign up on Eventbrite.
evidence: Ranch Camp's home page now shows its winter layout and no ladies ride; the record's 2026 series ran every other Monday from Jun 1, with Sep 28 the last listed date (fetched Oct 1, 2026). The ride page itself did not load.

name: Eastside Tours Evening Ride
schedule: Thursdays at 6:20 pm (briefing, then roll out); winter location is the east parking lot of Crossroads Park. First ride of each month is burrito night.

start_location.name: Crossroads Park, east parking lot (enter off 164th)

pace: Brisk, 16-18 mph on the flat; mellow on flats, hills at your own pace; about 1,500 ft of climbing

host.name: Cascade Bicycle Club Free Group Rides

visitor_notes: Front and rear lights required once it's dark. Free, but register on Cascade's site and attend the safety briefing. Go/no-go call is made at 4:20 pm on rough weather. A hilly ride.
description: A Thursday evening Cascade free group ride around the Eastside, with a different route each week and about 25 miles with 1,500 feet of climbing. It's brisk on the flat and climbs are at your own pace. First ride of each month finishes at Chipotle.
evidence: Cascade's ride calendar lists the Eastside Tours Evening Ride (winter location, part of the Eastside Tours series) for Thu Oct 1, 2026 at 6:20 pm with 15 spots (fetched Oct 1, 2026); only the Oct 1 date was posted.

refresh.notes: Series ride posted about a week ahead; confirm the next Thursday is listed.

name: Rabbit Ride
schedule: Every Sunday since 2011; 8:00 am during daylight saving time (roughly March through October), 8:30 am in standard time
pace: 16+ mph; groups leave by speed, fastest last
description: A self-organized Sunday road ride down Chuckanut Drive and back by Lake Samish. Groups roll out by pace, slowest first, fastest five minutes later. The shop is just the meeting spot and does not run it. Show up ready to ride at the start time.
evidence: Mount Baker Bicycle Club's event calendar lists the Rabbit Ride for Sundays Oct 4, 11, 18 and 25, 2026 at 8:00 AM, and its Weekly Rides page says 8 a.m. during daylight saving time (roughly March through October) and 8:30 a.m. in standard time; the old 7:45 / 8:15 times were on a March 1 entry.

name: Saturday Donut Ride
schedule: Every Saturday, every week of the year. Leaves Trek Bellingham at 7:30 am October through February and 7:00 am March through September.

start_location.name: Trek Bellingham (in front of the store)

pace: 17+ mph average, segments at 19+; three sprints with a regroup

host.name: Saturday Donut Ride (self-organized; listed by the Mount Baker Bicycle Club)

visitor_notes: Not a club ride and not insured by the club. It's a drop ride, though the group tries to stay together. Ask riders where the sprints are if you're new. Goes to Birch Bay and back.
description: Bellingham's long-running Saturday road ride, about 50 miles to Birch Bay and back at a fast pace. The club's calendar says it runs every week of the year, rain or shine. It's self-organized, so the group is whoever shows up.
evidence: Mount Baker Bicycle Club's event calendar lists the Saturday Donut Ride for Oct 3, 10, 17, 24 and 31, 2026 at 7:30 am from Trek Bellingham, 100 E Chestnut St (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

refresh.notes: Calendar lists each Saturday; the 7:00 am March start applies from March 2027.

name: Saturday Gravel Ride Series
schedule: Saturday series, gather 9:30-9:45 am, roll out 10:00 am sharp from Fairhaven Village Green. Posted for Oct 3 and Oct 24, 2026.
pace: Group pace; regroups after climbs and at important intersections
cost: free for a first ride; club membership after that
visitor_notes: Registration is required, including for non-members, who can come once to try it. The club asks you to join to be covered by its insurance.
description: A club-led, no-drop gravel ride that starts at the Fairhaven Village Green. The leaders regroup after climbs and at intersections so nobody gets lost. Dates are posted a few weeks at a time, with Oct 3 and Oct 24 up now.
evidence: Mount Baker Bicycle Club's calendar lists the Saturday Gravel Ride Series for Oct 3 and Oct 24, 2026, 10:00 am to noon, from the Fairhaven Village Green (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

refresh.notes: Only some Saturdays carry the series; look for 'Saturday Gravel Ride Series' on the calendar.

name: Shifting Gears Women's Mountain Bike Ride
status_note: The host's 2026 program ran Mondays May through September 2026 (last ride Sept 28). No fall or 2027 dates are posted yet.
schedule: Mondays, 5:30–7:30 pm, May through September

start_location.name: Galbraith Mountain or Lake Padden trailheads (varies weekly)

description: A weekly Monday evening trail ride for women 18 and up, whatever their experience, body size or nerves. Groups are capped at eight riders with two leaders. Rides go on Galbraith Mountain or at Lake Padden. Register ahead; sign-ups open two weeks before each ride.
evidence: Shifting Gears' mountain biking page lists weekly Monday rides from May 2026 through September 2026, with the last dated ride on Sept 28; no October or 2027 dates are posted.

name: Wednesday Winter Trail Ride (with lights)
schedule: Wednesdays, meet 5:45 pm, leave 6:00 pm, fall and winter. Starts late September or mid-October each year. Lights required.

start_location.name: Depot Market parking lot, across from Boundary Bay Brewery

pace: Moderate; the group stays together on the trails
visitor_notes: Bring front and rear lights. A cyclocross or trail-ready bike works. Road tires aren't great. Register on the club's event page; non-members can sign up at no fee.
description: The Mount Baker Bicycle Club's fall and winter Wednesday night ride on the trails, about 90 minutes with lights. It leaves from the Depot Market lot downtown. Cyclocross and old steel mountain bikes are fine.
evidence: Mount Baker Bicycle Club's calendar lists the Wednesday Workout Trail Ride (winter schedule, with lights) for Oct 7, 14, 21 and 28, 2026 at 6:00 pm (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

refresh.notes: Calendar lists each Wednesday.

name: Issaquah Social
schedule: Thursdays at 11:00 am from Issaquah (Oct 1: Tibbetts Valley Skateboard Park). Steady pace.
pace: Steady, 12-14 mph; the two posted rides ran 26 to 28 miles, hills climbed at a steady effort with regroups at the top

host.name: Cascade Bicycle Club Free Group Rides

visitor_notes: Free, but sign in on Cascade's site and register for each ride. Helmet and a safety briefing at the start are required.
description: A Thursday late-morning Cascade free group ride out of Issaquah. The Oct 1 route ran northwest to Bellevue College and Redmond and back on the East Lake Sammamish Trail, with a food stop at mile 16.6. It's a steady, social pace with regroups at the top of the hills.
evidence: Cascade's ride calendar lists Issaquah Social for Thu Oct 1 and Thu Oct 8, 2026 at 11:00 am (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

refresh.notes: Cascade posts each ride about a week ahead; check the start place.

name: MUMPS (Monday Urban Merry Pedalers)
schedule: Mondays, 10:00 am, from Log Boom Park in Kenmore, in three pace groups (Steady, Moderate, Brisk). Routes loop the north end of Lake Washington and Mercer Island, 26 to 50 miles. Some rides start at 9:00; check the posting.
pace: Steady (12–14 mph), Moderate (14–16 mph) and Brisk groups; frequent regroups, but leaders won't wait long for anyone well off the pace

host.name: Cascade Bicycle Club Free Group Rides

cost: free; register for each ride on Cascade's site
description: A Monday-morning Cascade free group ride from Log Boom Park, at the north tip of Lake Washington, on loops around the lake and Mercer Island. Three pace groups each week. Free, but register on Cascade's site first, wear a helmet and be there for the safety briefing.

name: Eastside Hills
schedule: Saturdays, year round, from the Kirkland Transit Center, in separate pace groups (Brisk, Strenuous, Vigorous). Each ride posts its own start time: 10:00 am in early October, 9:00 am in late August. A new hilly route east of Lake Washington each week.
pace: Brisk most weeks, sometimes Vigorous (18–20 mph on the flat) or faster; 3,000 to 4,000 ft of climbing

host.name: Cascade Bicycle Club Free Group Rides

cost: free; register for each ride on Cascade's site
description: Cascade's hill ride for strong riders: 50 to 60 miles east of Lake Washington with 3,000 to 4,000 feet of climbing, from the Kirkland Transit Center. Each pace is its own group, and regroups are occasional, at the tops of hills. Free, but register on Cascade's site first, wear a helmet and be there for the safety briefing.

name: Gravel Happy Hour
schedule: Second and fourth Sundays, October through March; meeting spot and time announced with each route
pace: two groups: a beginner ride and a faster ride

host.name: Cascadia Super Gravel with Big Stump Bikes and Olympia Mountain Bike Ride Club

description: Off-season gravel rides in Capitol Forest, two a month. One is a beginner ride led by the Olympia Mountain Bike Ride Club. The other is faster and led by Big Stump Bikes. Routes and meeting spots are posted before each ride.

name: Wednesday Chehalis Western Trail Ride
schedule: Every Wednesday at 9:00 am from the Chambers Lake Chehalis Western Trailhead in Lacey (the club's calendar says be ready to leave at 9:30).
pace: Easy, flat paved trail; Strava rates it Beginner / Flat
visitor_notes: From I-5 take exit 108 to Sleater Kinney Road SE south to 14th Ave, then left after the trestle. Bring money for the stop. Waiver required.
description: A 40-mile out-and-back on the Chehalis Western Trail that starts in Lacey and usually goes to Tenino, sometimes Yelm. It's flat, paved and social, with a stop on the way.
evidence: TWBC's Strava event page lists Wednesday Chehalis Western Trail for Wed Oct 7, 2026 at 9:00 am from 3725 14th Ave SE, rated Beginner / Flat (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

refresh.notes: Strava shows 9:00 am; the club's Google calendar text (2025) says leave at 9:30.

pace: Easy, flat paved trail; Strava rates it Beginner / Flat

description: One of TWBC's most popular weekly rides: a flat, paved run up the Foothills Trail to South Prairie for a drink, or on to Buckley for lunch. About 30 miles round trip to South Prairie, 40 to Buckley.
evidence: TWBC's Strava event page lists Thursdays Foothills Trail for Thu Oct 8, 2026 at 9:00 am from the East Puyallup Trailhead, rated Beginner / Flat (fetched Oct 1, 2026); the club calendar's wording says before 9:30.

refresh.notes: Strava shows 9:00 am; the club's Google calendar text (2025) says arrive before 9:30. Confirm if the time changes.

name: ROAD: Ride On After Dark
schedule: Wednesdays, 6:00 pm, through the winter, from the plaza between the Redmond Senior & Community Center and the police station. Five pace groups, Steady to Strenuous, on rotating routes of about 21 to 24 miles. A good headlight and red taillight are required.

start_location.name: Redmond Senior & Community Center (plaza by the police station)

pace: Five groups: Steady (12–14 mph), Moderate, Brisk, Vigorous and Strenuous; 1,340 to 1,600 ft of climbing; short regroups at the tops of hills

host.name: Cascade Bicycle Club Free Group Rides

cost: free; register for each ride on Cascade's site
description: Cascade's winter night training ride: every Wednesday evening out of Redmond, about 21 to 24 hilly miles in five pace groups. Lights front and rear are required. Groups don't stop for mechanicals, and a rider who can't hold the pace may finish alone. Free, but register on Cascade's site first and be there for the safety briefing.

name: TREATS (Tuesday Ride for Eclectic Athletic Travelers)
schedule: Tuesdays, 10:00 am; the start and route change each week, mostly on the Eastside. Steady pace.

start_location.name: Varies by week (Oct 6, 2026: Redmond; Jul 14, 2026: Redmond Ridge QFC, 23471 NE Novelty Hill Rd)

duration: about 4 to 5 hours, with a lunch or coffee stop
pace: Steady, 12–14 mph; hilly routes; keep the group in sight, with occasional regroups at the top of climbs

host.name: Cascade Bicycle Club Free Group Rides

cost: free; register for each ride on Cascade's site
description: A Tuesday Cascade free group ride at a steady pace, with a new start and route each week, often out to the Snoqualmie Valley with a lunch or coffee stop. Riders are asked to stay within sight of the group; the sweep won't stay with a rider far off the pace. Free, but register on Cascade's site first, wear a helmet and be there for the safety briefing.

name: Beer Junction Bike Club
schedule: Last Saturday of every month, meet and leave shortly after 2:00 pm from the back parking lot of The Beer Junction. Next: Oct 31, 2026.
pace: Easy, under 10 mph; 3-8 miles; rotating ride leaders and a new route each time
visitor_notes: Ages 21+. Helmets required. All bodies and all bikes welcome. Rain or shine.
description: A monthly beer-paced loop around West Seattle that starts and ends at The Beer Junction. Rides are led by a rotating group of experienced riders and run 4 to 10 miles at a slow pace, about 30 to 60 minutes. Bring a helmet and an ID.
evidence: The host's Everyday Rides series page says active every month on the last Saturday and lists the next ride for Sat Oct 31, 2026 at 2:00 pm, with 5 past rides (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

refresh.notes: Series page lists the next date.

name: COGS Wednesday Evening Ride
schedule: Wednesday evenings, year round, 5:45 pm to about 8:00 pm. Start place and route are posted by Monday or Tuesday if rain threatens.
pace: Evening exercise ride; pace set per ride
cost: free for one guest ride; membership from $25 a year

description: The club's weekly evening exercise ride around Seattle, held year round. Each week's start and route go up on the club calendar. Guests get one ride to try the club before joining.
evidence: COGS' own calendar lists the Wednesday evening ride for Oct 7, 2026, 5:45 to 8:00 pm, with 15 spaces left, and says there are rides on Wednesday evenings year round (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

refresh.notes: Home page lists the next few rides; the start place is added to each event during the week.

name: Critical Mass Seattle
schedule: Last Friday of every month, meet 6:30 pm at Westlake Park; the route is picked on the night
visitor_notes: Open to anyone. Bring lights. The ride's own posts are on Instagram.
description: The monthly Seattle Critical Mass starts at Westlake Park. The route is decided on the night. It usually has three legs: a start at Westlake, a grocery stop, and a finish at a park such as Golden Gardens or Discovery Park.
evidence: Seattle Bike Blog (Jan 29, 2026) says the ride meets at 6:30 pm at Westlake Park on the last Friday of the month, 'as always'; The Seattle Times' Ticket gives the same schedule (fetched Oct 2, 2026).

refresh.notes: Schedule comes from news pages; the group posts on Instagram, which does not load for a robot. A person should confirm the last Friday of the month.

name: FRUMPS (Friday Rides for Underemployed Merry Pedalers)
schedule: Fridays, about 10:00 am (some weeks a 9:15 early start); start place changes each week. Steady pace, 12-14 mph.

start_location.name: Varies by week (Oct 2: Matthews Beach Park; Oct 9: Woodinville; Oct 16: West Seattle)

pace: Steady, 12-14 mph, regroups at hilltops and turns; the three posted rides ran 32 to 35 miles

host.name: Cascade Bicycle Club Free Group Rides

visitor_notes: Free, but sign in on Cascade's site and register for each ride. Helmets and a safety briefing at the start are required; bring a spare tube and fenders in the wet.
description: A weekday-morning Cascade free group ride, led by volunteers, at a steady pace across Seattle and the north end. Each Friday brings a new route and start. Expect coffee and snack stops along the way.
evidence: Cascade's ride calendar lists FRUMPS for Fri Oct 2, Oct 9 and Oct 16, 2026 (10:00 am, 10:00 am and 9:15 am) as part of the Friday series (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

refresh.notes: Cascade posts each week's ride about a week ahead; the start place changes weekly.

name: Good Weather Sunday Social
schedule: Every Sunday, 10:30 am to about 2:00 pm
description: An all-inclusive casual ride from Tailwind Cafe on Capitol Hill with rotating leaders and a new route each week. Park sits and pastry stops are part of the plan. Rain or shine; ice or snow cancels.
evidence: Everyday Rides' series page shows the ride active every Sunday with upcoming dates Oct 4, 11 and 18, 2026, 10:30 am to 2:00 pm from Tailwind Cafe, leisurely 10-12 mph, stay together.

name: LUMPS (Leisurely Urbane Matthews-beach Pedalers)
schedule: Wednesdays, late morning. The posted rides have two starts: Matthews Beach Park in North Seattle at 11:30 am (Steady) and the East Lake Sammamish Trail by the Redmond Whole Foods at 11:10 am (Moderate). Both ride flat trails to a pie stop in Bothell.
pace: Steady (12–14 mph) from Matthews Beach; Moderate (14–16 mph) from Redmond; flat trail riding, a social ride

host.name: Cascade Bicycle Club Free Group Rides

description: Cascade's Wednesday social ride on the flat trails north of the lake, built around a pie or cookie stop at the North Shore Senior Center in Bothell. One group leaves Matthews Beach Park, another leaves Redmond. Free, but register on Cascade's site first, wear a helmet and be there for the safety briefing; e-bikes welcome at these paces.

name: Mello Fellos Saturday Ride

description: A shop ride that starts and ends at Mello Fellos on Sixth Avenue. Ride leaders take a Mello route around the city, with views of Puget Sound, Lake Union, Discovery Park, the UW campus or Lake Washington. The pace is friendly and most rides run 15 to 25 miles.
evidence: Everyday Rides lists the shop's Saturday ride for Oct 17 and Oct 24, 2026 at 8:00 am from 2151 Sixth Ave, and the shop's Strava club says Saturday mornings at 8:00 am (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

name: Moxie Monday

description: A ride for women, trans, femme and non-binary riders on any kind of bike. Casual pace, frequent regroups and breaks, usually under 20 miles. Meets at Westlake Park. The same crew runs an annual W/T/F alley cat.
evidence: Everyday Rides' Moxie Monday group page lists the monthly reboot ride for Mon Oct 5, Nov 2 and Dec 7, 2026 at 6:00 pm from Westlake Park (first Monday of the month, women / trans / femme / nonbinary).

description: A Sunday no-drop ride organized by and for Black, Brown and Indigenous riders in Seattle. Easy pace, rolls from the club's Central District clubhouse. The club's stated aim is to take down barriers to cycling and support riders' physical and mental health. All bikes welcome.

name: WTFNB Weekly with Brevay

name: Bicycle Butler Wednesday Ride

description: A weekly shop ride led by Bicycle Butler's mechanics and friends. New riders welcome, all bike types including e-bikes. The route changes weekly and gets posted by noon on Wednesday. Runs year-round; lights required in fall and early spring. Helmets required.

name: Spokane Bicycle Club Monday Riverside State Park Ride

name: Spokane Bicycle Club Team Thursday
schedule: Thursdays, meet 9:15 am, roll 9:30 am. Start place changes (Oct 1: Safeway on N Newport Hwy). Mid-March to mid-November.

visitor_notes: Helmets required and the club waiver applies. Rain, high winds or other extreme conditions may cancel; check Meetup. The Oct 1 address is only that week's start.

evidence: The club's Meetup feed lists Team Thursday for Thu Oct 1, 2026 at 9:30 am (meet 9:15), and the Meetup past events show a Team Thursday ride on Sept 24 (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

schedule: Fridays, arrive 9:45 am for a briefing, depart 10:00 am. Women only. Start place changes each week; mid-March to mid-November.

visitor_notes: Book on Rapha's events site. The page does not say the ride is members-only.

name: Critical Mass Hamburg

evidence: criticalmass.in logs the Sept 25, 2026 ride at the Alter Elbpark with an estimated 1,315 riders over 24.4 km; the Aug 28 (1,134 riders) and Jul 31 (1,788 riders) rides are logged the same way (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

pace: Mass pace, set by the crowd
visitor_notes: Free, no sign-up and no leader. Numbers swing with the season: about 25 riders in June 2026, 246 in September. Bring lights.

start_location.name: Max-Josef-Platz, in front of the Opera (by Odeonsplatz)

visitor_notes: No sign-up. Use the Critical Maps app if you miss the start. Children are welcome.
description: Munich's monthly Critical Mass. Riders meet in front of the Opera, roll out together and the group has no organizer. The site says all are welcome, alone, in groups or with children.

name: Killakee Viewpoint (Thursday evening)

evidence: Dublin Easy Wheelers' Meetup lists this ride for Thu Sept 24 and the upcoming Thu Oct 1, 2026, 6:30 pm (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

name: PPA Weekly Social Rides

start_location.name: 9 Hill Park Lane, Mowbray
start_location.address: 9 Hill Park Lane, Mowbray, Cape Town
